PullRequest.Title: sandbox: add sandbox profiles stored on the agent host
PullRequest.Body:
Adds **sandbox profiles**: named sets of agent sandbox settings stored on an agent host. Every client connected to that host sees and can change them, so the same profile is available when you continue working on a host from another device.

## What changed

**Agent Host**
- Two new root config keys in `sandboxConfigSchema`: `sandboxProfiles` (profile ID → `{ name, sandbox }`) and `activeSandboxProfile`. They are separate keys so switching the active profile never rewrites the profiles. Writes are validated against the existing sandbox schema, persisted to `agent-host-config.json`, and broadcast to all clients through the existing `root/configChanged`.
- `getRootSandboxConfig()` resolves a session's base sandbox settings as the host's `sandbox` values with the active profile on top. Session overrides and managed policy still apply afterwards, so policy always wins. An unknown active profile falls back to the `sandbox` values.
- Running sessions pick up an active-profile change the same way they pick up any root sandbox change today.

**Sandbox: Manage Sandbox Profiles** (Command Palette) opens a modal editor for one host. With more than one connected host that supports profiles, it asks which.
- Profile list with **Use for New Sessions**, **Edit Profile**, and **Delete Profile**; the active profile shows an **Active** badge.
- New profiles are named `sandbox_profile_N` and start from the current VS Code sandbox settings. Saved profiles open read-only until **Edit** is selected.
- **User-Configured Paths** uses an inline JSON editor with schema completions and validation; Save is blocked while it is invalid.
- Deleting the active profile also clears it, so new sessions never silently fall back.
- Read-only when the host is disconnected or does not advertise sandbox profiles.
- Accessibility help (Alt+F1) and a verbosity setting.

**Agents: Manage Remote Environments** gains a **Sandbox Profile** column. Its dropdown (**Default** or one of the host's profiles) sets the host's active profile and is disabled while a host is disconnected.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Last write wins.** Profiles target continuity (one person moving between devices), so concurrent edits are not merged.
- **Reconnecting never replaces a selection.** `AgentHostSandboxForwarder` is unchanged from `main`: it only writes the `sandbox` key and never the profile keys, so a client that reconnects (for example, a laptop waking from sleep) cannot undo a change made from another device.
- **Interop:** clients treat a host as supporting profiles only when its root config schema advertises both keys (`readHostSandboxProfiles` in `platform/agentHost/common/sandboxProfiles.ts`). The keys are host-defined root config; no protocol change.
- The editor keeps its values keyed by VS Code setting ID and converts to the host's sandbox keys only when reading and saving.
- Fixes **Add Item** showing on read-only string lists: the Settings rule that hides it is scoped to the Settings editor.

## Tests and covered scenarios

- `sessionSandbox.test.ts`: the active profile overrides host values; omitted keys fall back; managed policy still wins; an unknown active ID falls back; malformed profiles are rejected by the schema.
- `sandboxProfiles.test.ts`: profiles saved on the host are visible to another client; unique default names and read-only saved profiles; duplicate names rejected; deleting the active profile clears it; changes from other clients refresh a read-only view without discarding an edit in progress; disconnected or unsupported hosts cannot be edited.
- `agentHostSandboxForwarder.test.ts`: a reconnecting client writes only `sandbox`, never the profile keys.
- `remotesWidget.test.ts`: the column sets and clears the host's active profile without connecting; the dropdown is disabled for disconnected hosts; navigation keys don't move table focus; hidden on non-remote rows.

Validated with TypeScript, oxlint, stylelint, the layer check, and the focused suites above. The editor was exercised manually in a Code OSS build against the local agent host: creating a profile, activating it, the persisted host config, and deleting the active profile.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The root subscription emits for every root action, active-turn tracking emits when a session becomes active or idle, and both new consumers synchronously refresh without checking profile changes. The editor explicitly disposes and recreates its CodeEditorWidget and model on each notification. Duration is not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CodeEditorWidget instances, JSON text models, settings controls, profile validation allocations, and select option DOM nodes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One full editor reconstruction per root event while the modal is open; a session transitioning idle→active→idle produces two such events, not one event per token or per chat in an already-active session. Each rendered remote-host row also rebuilds its host's P+1 options per event.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Avoidable synchronous UI work and allocation/GC pressure during background agent activity, causing editing or table interaction to stutter.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Session activity and terminal-list changes did not perform any sandbox-profile UI reconstruction; neither this watcher nor the profile controls existed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: An unrelated root/activeSessionsChanged, root/terminalsChanged, or root configuration update now invokes the profile callbacks even when profiles and the active selection are unchanged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added rootState.onDidChange(() => onChange()) at line 60 connects all root actions, rather than changes to the profile keys, to the newly added refresh paths.
Findings.Title: Filter unrelated root changes before refreshing profile controls
Findings.Impact: Leaving Manage Sandbox Profiles open while another client runs turns on the same host causes repeated heavyweight editor reconstruction despite no profile changes. The Remote Environments table likewise repeatedly rebuilds the affected host's dropdown.
Findings.Evidence: RootStateSubscription._isRelevantEnvelope accepts every root/* action (agentSubscription.ts:303-304), and BaseAgentSubscription._reconcile fires onDidChange (287). AgentHostStateManager._addChatActiveTurn/_removeChatActiveTurn dispatch active-count updates on session activity transitions (3271, 3284). SandboxProfilesInput._onDidChangeHost fires onDidSelect even for an unchanged saved profile or an edit in progress (170-182). SandboxProfilesEditor.setInput wires that event to _render (250); _render clears all controls and DOM (354-359), then _jsonRow recreates CodeEditorWidget, schema registration, and model (477-502). RemotesTableRenderer.refresh also creates fresh option objects (543), defeating SelectBoxList.setOptions' reference-based array comparison (selectBoxCustom.ts:304-312).
Findings.Recommendation: Track host availability/capability, the profiles value, and active selection and notify only when these actually change, resetting the comparison on reconnect. Keep ordinary activity/terminal/root-config updates out of these refresh paths.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: getRootValue has no validation cache and invokes the recursive schema assertion for every read. The new call always reads the entire profiles bag before checking the active ID, and traced callers run before turns and shell permission decisions. Exact list sizes and elapsed time are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Recursive schema-validation CPU work and temporary property-path strings/arrays for the entire profiles bag
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Adds O(P×F+L) validation per root sandbox read, with P saved profiles, fixed F sandbox fields, and L total domain/path/credential entries across all profiles. This repeats across turns and shell checks, even with a warm unchanged configuration or no active profile; some SDK config computations perform two root reads.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased agent-host CPU and allocation/GC work on the critical path before starting turns or approving shell tools.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each sandbox resolution validated only the host's sandbox values and session overrides; the cost was independent of saved inactive profiles.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every sandbox resolution now recursively validates every saved profile, including every configured domain/path array, before using at most one profile or none.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added getRootValue(sandboxConfigSchema, SandboxProfiles) at line 22 is evaluated unconditionally by getRootSandboxConfig, including when ActiveSandboxProfile is unset, and replaces the old single Sandbox property read in getSessionSandboxConfig.
Findings.Title: Avoid revalidating all saved profiles on every sandbox read
Findings.Impact: Hosts keeping several sandbox variants with substantial domain or path lists pay to validate all inactive variants for every turn and shell-policy check; selecting Default does not remove this overhead.
Findings.Evidence: AgentConfigurationService.getRootValue (1288-1305) calls schema.assertValid on every invocation without caching. agentHostSchema.buildAssert (207-253) walks object additionalProperties, nested sandbox properties, and every array element. getRootSandboxConfig now reads SandboxProfiles unconditionally; resolveRootSandboxConfig only subsequently selects the active entry. CopilotAgentSession._prepareSdkTurn awaits sandbox.applyConfig (7755), which computes the config before serialized-config deduplication (copilotSessionSandbox.ts:550, 568-572). Shell permissions call isShellSandboxedByDefault (copilotAgentSession.ts:9286), whose SDK path computes the config (copilotSessionSandbox.ts:377); the custom engine also resolves it for each getSandboxSetting (agentHostSandboxEngine.ts:132).
Findings.Recommendation: Read the active ID first and skip profiles entirely for Default. For active profiles, reuse validated values until the raw profiles value changes, with invalidation on profile replacement and proper handling of invalid/missing values, rather than rescanning the bag for every setting read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Manage Sandbox Profiles, select a host/profile, and edit settings or view accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Host selection uses existing connection/root-state snapshots. Opening the modal synchronously reads profiles, builds settings controls, constructs one inline JSON editor/model, and lays out the content before interaction. Accessibility help is generated only on request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the selected paths object and create its text model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected-profile JSON model per render, proportional to its path-document size, not P models
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This modal and its inline document did not exist; opening this new feature legitimately adds one initial construction
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stringification and model/editor construction run synchronously before the modal can be used

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schema and association changes are published through the existing virtual filesystem provider; an active JSON client can refresh associations and notify its language server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One schema/association for the inline paths document; association refreshes within 500 ms are coalesced by the JSON client
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing registry/client mechanism was present, but this modal did not register a schema or association
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Language-service refresh is off the initial synchronous UI critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H connected hosts are checked by the command; the chosen host has P saved profiles and L total validated entries. Only the selected profile's JSON document and settings controls are instantiated; the sidebar list virtualizes rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host enumeration and UI construction are synchronous. There is no per-profile remote operation. JSON language-service work is asynchronous; schema-association refresh is debounced for 500 ms by the existing JSON client.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root state is already cached; enumeration does not fetch each profile. Pane construction is deferred until opening, but profile getters revalidate the bag without a validation cache. Models/schema registrations are disposed on reconstruction or clearInput, rather than retained indefinitely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the command reads snapshots and editor construction is explicit. Initial construction is intentional; the regression is its unrelated-event repetition, covered separately.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Initial latency depends on host count, profile list size, selected JSON size, and whether the JSON language service is already active.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate initial-opening or accessibility regression: heavyweight UI is created on explicit feature use, not at registration/startup. Disposal ownership is present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep the profiles modal open while another client starts or finishes agent turns on the same host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Incoming root envelopes synchronously emit rootState.onDidChange. The new watcher invokes SandboxProfilesInput._onDidChangeHost, which emits onDidSelect even for unchanged profiles; the pane immediately disposes and reconstructs all controls and its JSON editor/model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver root/activeSessionsChanged envelopes to connected clients
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two envelopes for an isolated session turn entering and leaving the active set; not per streamed token
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same envelopes were already delivered, but did not reconstruct sandbox-profile controls
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery now triggers synchronous heavyweight profile UI work on the receiving renderer

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose and recreate the selected JSON document and CodeEditorWidget, stringifying paths again
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete editor/model rebuild per unrelated root event while the modal has an input
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No profile editor/model reconstruction occurred on these session activity events
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous construction/layout consumes the renderer thread during interaction

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E root events on the selected host; idle-to-active and active-to-idle transitions each produce one event per session. Concurrent chats within an already-active session do not each generate count transitions. Work per event includes all-profile validation, sidebar updates, and selected-document reconstruction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI callbacks run serially on the renderer thread; events are not filtered/coalesced before reconstruction. Backend sessions can independently cause events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached root snapshots do not prevent callbacks. Unchanged profiles are checked but still emit onDidSelect. Existing controls/models are discarded rather than reused. Association refresh is debounced downstream, but synchronous pane reconstruction is not.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: root emission, the unconditional watcher, unchanged-profile notifications, and full reconstruction were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Stutter duration depends on event frequency and document/list size; no frame timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported medium-severity repeated UI work at sandboxProfiles.ts:60. Performance impact is independent of any focus or stale-state correctness consequences.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse Remote Environments and use its Sandbox Profile dropdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendered remote rows create a SelectBox, attach disposable connection/root listeners, validate that host's profiles, and build options. Selecting an option dispatches one active-profile update without connecting or fetching profiles individually.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch root/configChanged containing the active profile ID or empty string
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per user selection; not one per option or saved profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No profile picker or active-profile update existed; other remote-table actions used their existing operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local dropdown handling is synchronous; persistence/broadcast and live-session synchronization follow host processing

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove/recreate native option DOM nodes from fresh option objects
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P+1 nodes per affected rendered host row per refresh, including unrelated root events
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The table had no profile dropdown and performed none of this option reconstruction
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the renderer during table interaction

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V rendered remote rows, bounded by table virtualization; each host contributes P+1 options. An event on one host refreshes that host's rendered rows, whereas connection-set changes invoke all V connection listeners.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes and option DOM creation run synchronously on the renderer. No subprocess, filesystem request, or per-profile network read occurs during row rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connection and profile data come from root snapshots. Fresh option objects defeat the select widget's reference-based array equality, so even unrelated host-root events rebuild options. Element/template disposal removes listeners, so no unbounded listener retention was established.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: table virtualization/disposal and exact dropdown refresh logic were inspected; no hidden profile fetch was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical visible host counts and profiles per host are unknown. The modal reconstruction is the more consequential manifestation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Unrelated-event option reconstruction shares the reported unfiltered-watcher root cause and is not duplicated as another finding. Required initial dropdown construction and one-action selection are not standalone regressions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, save, delete, or activate host profiles; propagate changes to other clients and reconnect
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The input validates its draft, converts the profiles collection for saves/deletes, and dispatches a root config action. The host validates/reduces it, emits changes, and serializes persistence. UI save does not await disk durability. Relevant live sessions synchronize effective sandbox config; reconnection retains host profile keys.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send profile config action to the host and broadcast resulting root changes to clients
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outbound action per operation and one resulting envelope per subscribed client when values change; full profile bag for save/delete, scalar for activation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Profile operations did not exist; the same root-config action transport already served ordinary sandbox/configuration updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host acceptance precedes remote clients seeing the values; local save itself does not await host persistence

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the root config, mkdir, write temporary file, and rename agent-host-config.json
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence job per processed profile action, containing the complete root config; jobs are serialized host-wide, not per profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The persistence mechanism already ran for ordinary root config updates; this diff adds explicit profile-operation callers and profile bytes
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stringification runs during host processing; asynchronous writes are queued and are not awaited by the profile editor's save

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update SDK session sandbox options after an effective host setting change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one options update per eligible session synchronization; zero when serialized effective config equals the last accepted config, including unchanged inactive-profile edits
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same synchronization/deduplication existed for ordinary sandbox changes; profile activation now changes the effective values through that path
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized within each session; applying required live policy can precede its next turn

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P profiles and total serialized profile bytes for save/delete; active-only actions carry one scalar. Broadcast scales with C connected root subscribers. SDK updates scale with eligible live SDK sessions whose effective config actually changes, not with P profiles.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Root-config filesystem writes use one host-wide promise chain. Sandbox RPCs use per-SDK-session sequencers; independent sessions can synchronize concurrently, with no newly introduced per-profile burst. User operations are explicit saves/selections, not keystroke persistence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root state is cached on each client. Server deep-equality no-op suppression avoids redundant root emissions. Existing SDK serialized-config comparison skips unchanged RPCs. The unchanged forwarder writes only sandbox on reconnect, preserving profile values and active selection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: action payload cardinality, server no-op suppression, persistence sequencing, and SDK deduplication were read directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profile bytes, connected client count, and live eligible session count vary. No evidence of problematic per-profile boundary fan-out was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: Persistence, shared broadcast, and changed-effective-policy synchronization are intentional feature work, not separate findings. Unfiltered client UI refresh is covered by the first finding; repeated runtime validation is covered by the second.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start/resume an agent session, start subsequent turns, or approve/run sandboxed shell tools with saved profiles
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session preparation resolves sandbox settings and existing path grants. Turn preparation awaits sandbox.applyConfig before the SDK turn starts. Shell permission checks resolve config before replying; custom shell wrapping reads individual settings before executing the command. The newly added full-profiles validation occurs before any warm SDK deduplication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted session sandbox path metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing read when live paths are unavailable for the owner; warm populated paths skip the read. No read per saved profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-path load and per-session sequencing occurred before profiles

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate application runtime directories to establish sandbox read roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on macOS/equal roots; otherwise at most two deduplicated readdir calls, then reused by the sandbox instance
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical application-root discovery and cache existed before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on cold prepare; warm preparation reuses roots

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One on a required changed/cold configuration; zero on unchanged warm configuration. Inactive profiles are not sent to the SDK
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC, per-session sequencer, and serialized-config deduplication existed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before turn launch when needed; new validation overhead is paid even when the RPC is skipped

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize effective terminal sandbox settings and create/overwrite its settings file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One when cold, forced, settings-invalidated, or command context changes; warm matching command context reuses the path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same terminal settings-file lifecycle existed; profiles alter effective settings rather than adding one file per profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before wrapping/executing a sandboxed custom shell command

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use an owned shell terminal and execute the wrapped command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing shell creation/reuse per shell lifecycle and command execution per shell tool, independent of saved profile count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shell ownership, terminal creation, wrapping, and execution paths were present
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Command execution follows sandbox checks/wrapping; added synchronous validation delays reaching it

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P saved profiles, fixed F sandbox properties, and L total array entries across all profiles, multiplied by sandbox reads across turns/tool checks. At most one profile is selected. SDK config computation can read root settings twice; the custom engine resolves config again for each requested setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation is synchronous host CPU work. Sandbox updates are sequenced per SDK session, independent across sessions. Path-store operations are sequenced per owning session. Application-directory enumeration uses Promise.all over at most two deduplicated directories. Shell execution uses existing shell ownership/busy-state management.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getRootValue recursively validates on every call without a validation cache, even for warm unchanged values and Default selection. SDK accepted-config caching skips RPC but not the preceding CPU work. Session path loading skips when live paths are present; workspace paths use in-memory host storage. Application read roots are retained after prepare. Terminal config files and dependency status have existing warm caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high for repeated validation: getRootValue's uncached assertion, recursive collection traversal, and important callers were directly traced. Existing boundary cache/ordering behavior was inspected separately.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CPU duration depends on saved profile count and their domain/path list sizes; severity is low because no measured slowdown or typical size distribution is available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported low-severity repeated-work regression at sessionSandbox.ts:22. Existing cached I/O/RPC/subprocess operations are not reported as newly introduced fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 19 changed files and all diff pages against base 60385084191c4017b47890036eabef4a92e1b570. Submitted two introduced regressions: unfiltered root-state events reconstruct profile UI, and sandbox reads repeatedly validate the entire inactive-profile collection. Inspected listener/model/schema disposal, lazy editor ownership, root persistence and broadcasts, SDK update deduplication, and session/workspace storage. No concrete removed performance regression qualified for fix-provenance collection. Static review; no measured timings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
